title: Quantifying and Bounding Spatiotemporal Correlations in Quantum Noise
abstract: Spatial and temporal correlations in quantum noise challenge the local Markovian models commonly used in quantum information processing. We develop a unified operational framework for quantifying temporal, spatial, and total spatiotemporal correlations in general quantum processes. Using process tensors, we define these quantities through optimal distinguishability from Markovian, spatially local, and fully uncorrelated processes. Optimization over admissible probing combs ensures monotonicity under every superprocess that preserves the corresponding free set, while Choi-state functionals and restricted probes provide accessible lower bounds. We establish hierarchy and interpolation relations among the correlation measures and derive dimension-dependent upper bounds on temporal correlations transmitted by quantum memories, with tighter bounds for classical memory, together with universal ceilings imposed by the system dimension. These bounds turn certified lower estimates into witnesses of minimum memory dimension, nonclassicality under a memory-dimension constraint, and inconsistencies in the assumed process model. We illustrate the results with effective superconducting-qubit models featuring \(ZZ\) and \(XY\) interactions, exhibiting saturation of classical-memory, quantum-memory, and system-dimension ceilings. These results pave the way toward practical approaches to characterizing and addressing spatiotemporally correlated errors in quantum devices.
summary: This paper introduces a unified, operational framework to quantify and bound complex spatiotemporal correlations in quantum noise processes. By defining correlations through optimal distinguishability from idealized noise models, the authors derive dimension-dependent upper bounds. These bounds are powerful diagnostic tools, enabling the certification of minimum memory dimensions and the detection of flawed process assumptions in quantum devices.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of quantifying and bounding spatiotemporal correlations present in quantum noise, which invalidate simple local Markovian models used in quantum information processing.
main_result: A unified operational framework is established that provides dimension-dependent upper bounds on temporal correlations, allowing these bounds to certify minimum memory dimensions or detect model inconsistencies.
method: The authors develop a framework using process tensors and define correlations via optimal distinguishability measures (like Choi divergences) from idealized process sets (Markovian, local, uncorrelated).
model_or_system: The theory is illustrated using effective superconducting-qubit models featuring ZZ and XY interactions, allowing for concrete testing of the derived bounds.
key_observables: Temporal, spatial, and total spatiotemporal correlations; minimum memory dimension; nonclassicality under memory constraints.
important_parameters: System dimension; interaction types (ZZ, XY); probing comb structure.
main_assumptions: The framework aims to overcome limitations of existing Choi-state divergences by using optimal operational distinguishability measures.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares standard, uncorrelated noise models against general spatiotemporally correlated noise using process tensors.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the general process tensor representation for multitime/multisystem noise, introduces the operational correlation functionals via Choi divergences, and then derives and tests the bounding relations using specific qubit models.
why_interesting: This work provides rigorous, resource-theoretic tools to characterize the complexity of noise in quantum hardware, which is crucial for designing fault-tolerant quantum memories and processors.
